# CNBC Daily Open: Trump's big threats and Big Tech's bigger wallets
Published Wed, Apr 29 2026
![thumbnail](https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/107342427-1701684837391-Lim_Hui_Jie.jpg?v=1701684958&w=60&h=60&ffmt=webp)
[Lim Hui Jie](https://www.cnbc.com/lim-hui-jie/)[@in/hui-jie-lim-a7371176/](https://linkedin.com/in/hui-jie-lim-a7371176/)
[WATCH LIVE](https://www.cnbc.com/live-tv/)
Key Points
  * Trump’s naval blockade vow sends Brent crude up 6% to $118.
  * Dow logs its fifth straight loss amid geopolitical uncertainty.
  * Fed holds rates at 3.5–3.75% in the most divided vote since 1992, Powell vows to remain on the board.
  * Big Tech earnings boom: results from Microsoft, Alphabet and Samsung.


US President Donald Trump looks on during a press conference about the conflict in Iran in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room of the White House on April 6, 2026, in Washington, DC.
Saul Loeb | Afp | Getty Images
_Taken from CNBC’s Daily Open, our international markets newsletter —[Subscribe today](https://www.cnbc.com/sign-up-for-cnbc-newsletters/)_
_Hello, this is Hui Jie writing to you from Singapore. Welcome to another edition of CNBC's Daily Open._
_Iran has returned to the headlines after U.S. President Donald Trump issued a fresh warning to Tehran — this time with a picture straight out of a James Bond film — while the Federal Reserve delivered its most divided decision in decades._
_Elsewhere, tech companies take the earnings spotlight, with Microsoft and Alphabet announcing massive capital spending, while Samsung Electronics reported record-breaking results._
##  What you need to know today
"Speak softly and carry a big stick," former U.S. President [Theodore Roosevelt famously said](https://www.theodorerooseveltcenter.org/quote/speak-softly-and-carry-a-big-stick-you-will-go-far-if-a-man-continually-blusters-if-he-lacks-civility-a-big-stick-will-not-save-him-from-trouble-and-neither-will-speaking-softly-avail-i/).
The current occupant of the White House, however, seems to prefer a different approach, as evidenced [on Truth Social](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/29/trump-iran-threat-ai-picture-gun-war-strait-of-hormuz.html).
Trump on Wednesday reiterated his threat to Iran, saying the [U.S. would maintain its naval blockade](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/29/oil-prices-brent-wti-trump-iran.html) until Tehran agrees to a nuclear deal — a message delivered with characteristic flair on social media.
The rhetoric rattled an already edgy oil market, sending the price of Brent crude up 6% to top $118 per barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures also climbed 1.05% to $108.
[Markets dipped](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/28/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) amid the uncertainty. The [Dow Jones Industrial Average](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.DJI/) notched its fifth straight day of losses.  
  
At the same time, [the Federal Reserve delivered](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/29/fed-interest-rate-decision-april-2026.html) its most divided decision since 1992 as it held rates steady at 3.5%-3.75%, in an 8-4 split.
While this may be Jerome Powell's last Fed meeting as chair, he has [vowed to stay](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/29/fed-meeting-today-live-updates-warsh-powell.html) on the board of governors, citing ongoing legal actions taken against him. 
Away from politics, earnings season provided a more upbeat narrative.
[Alphabet beat expectations](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/29/alphabet-googl-q1-2026-earnings.html) with 20% revenue growth and raised its capital expenditure outlook to as much as $190 billion for 2026, with more to come in 2027. [Microsoft also topped forecasts](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/29/microsoft-msft-q3-earnings-report-2026.html), though it warned of soaring memory costs as spending climbs toward levels similar to those of Alphabet. 
In Asia, [Samsung Electronics posted](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/30/samsung-q1-earnings-ai-memory-chip-demand-profit-record.html) an over eightfold increase in first-quarter operating profits, hitting a new record and surpassing analysts' estimates.
To paraphrase Roosevelt: Big Tech may not be speaking softly, but it is definitely carrying a very big wallet.
_— Lim Hui Jie_
##  And finally...
[**Anthropic in talks with investors to raise funds at $900 billion valuation, higher than OpenAI**](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/04/29/anthropic-weighs-raising-funds-at-900b-valuation-topping-openai.html)
Anthropic has been chasing OpenAI since the launch of ChatGPT in late 2022. It appears to have finally caught up.
The [artificial intelligence](https://www.cnbc.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/) startup, founded five years ago by former OpenAI execs, is in talks with investors to raise money at a $900 billion valuation, according to a person familiar with the matter. 
OpenAI was valued at [$852 billion](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/31/openai-funding-round-ipo.html) in late March after closing a record-breaking $122 billion funding round. Large contributions came from strategic investors, including up to $50 billion from [Amazon](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/AMZN/), $30 billion from [Nvidia](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/NVDA/) and $30 billion from SoftBank.
_— Kate Rooney, Ashley Capoot_
